scene.note: You write the lines of Notice.java, the compiler checks every one, and only then does main run and print the notice.

steps.note: Bridie wants the welcome at the top of the notice, exactly as the task spells it.
Under Task 1 you add one statement that prints it, with the text in double quotes.
The compiler reads the whole file first. A missing semicolon or quote stops it here.
Once every line is accepted, main runs and the welcome shows on a line of its own.
The crossing times are two lines, and Bridie wants them in the order the task gives.
Each line gets its own print, one under the other.
main runs its statements from top to bottom.
The terminal shows the two lines, one right after the other.
The hut's hours are printed in two parts, and today each part ends its own line.
One way of printing ends the line, the other leaves it open for what comes next.
The two parts come out on one line, and that line ends after the second part.
A statement under Task 4 still prints the free bicycles notice Ossian stopped.
The compiler skips every comment, so a line turned into one no longer runs.
The old notice no longer prints, and the line stays in the file in case it comes back.
